questions.question: Dr. Mourad wishes to hire a dental assistant. According to Article 6 of the Labor Code, what is an employee?
options: Any person who exercises their activity under the direction of an employer in exchange for remuneration
Any person who works independently without a subordinate relationship
Any person who holds a university degree
Any person who manages their own dental practice
questions.explanation: Article 6 defines the employee as any person who has undertaken to exercise their professional activity under the direction of one or more employers in exchange for remuneration.

questions.question: According to Article 6 of the Labor Code, who is considered an employer?
options: Any person who hires the services of one or more natural persons
Any patient who consults a dentist
Any employee who receives a salary
Any union representative in the company
questions.explanation: Article 6 defines the employer as any natural or legal person, private or public, who hires the services of one or more natural persons.

questions.question: Dr. Sidki wishes to hire an assistant on a permanent contract. According to Article 16, what is the general principle for the duration of the employment contract?
options: The contract is concluded for an indefinite period by default
The contract is always concluded for a fixed term
The contract must be renewed each month
The contract cannot exceed one year
questions.explanation: Article 16 provides that the employment contract is concluded for an indefinite period, for a fixed term, or to perform a specific job, the principle being the indefinite period.

questions.question: Dr. Mourad wishes to replace an assistant on maternity leave. According to Article 16, what type of contract can he conclude?
questions.explanation: Article 16 provides for the fixed-term contract particularly in the case of replacing an employee in the event of suspension of the employment contract.

questions.question: According to Article 14, what is the maximum probation period for an employee (dental assistant)?
questions.explanation: Article 14 sets the probation period at one and a half months for employees, renewable once.

questions.question: Dr. Sidki wishes to hire a manager for his practice. According to Article 14, what is the maximum probation period?
questions.explanation: Article 14 sets the probation period at three months for managers and equivalent positions, renewable once.

questions.question: According to Article 14, the probation period for fixed-term contracts cannot exceed:
options: 15 days for contracts under 6 months and 1 month for those over 6 months
questions.explanation: Article 14 provides that the probation period for fixed-term contracts cannot exceed one day per week of work, up to a limit of two weeks for contracts under 6 months, and one month for those over 6 months.

questions.question: According to Article 13, can Dr. Mourad terminate the probation period of his new assistant without notice?
options: Yes, without any formalities throughout the period
Yes, but after one week, a notice period of 2 or 8 days is required depending on the pay period
No, termination must always be justified
Yes, but only with the employee's agreement
questions.explanation: Article 13 specifies that if termination occurs after at least one week of work, a notice period of 2 days (daily/weekly pay) or 8 days (monthly pay) is required.

questions.question: Dr. Sidki wishes to dismiss an assistant for gross misconduct. According to Article 39, which act is considered gross misconduct?
options: Deliberate refusal to perform work within their competence
questions.explanation: Article 39 lists gross misconduct, including notably the deliberate and unjustified refusal of the employee to perform work within their competence.

questions.question: According to Article 39, an unjustified absence of the employee for more than how many days constitutes gross misconduct?
questions.explanation: Article 39 considers as gross misconduct the unjustified absence of the employee for more than four days or eight half-days over a twelve-month period.

questions.question: According to Article 62, before a dismissal for gross misconduct, Dr. Mourad must:
options: Give the employee the opportunity to defend themselves and be heard
Only ask for the union's opinion
questions.explanation: Article 62 requires that the employee be able to defend themselves and be heard by the employer before dismissal, in the presence of the employee delegate or union representative.

questions.question: According to Article 35, dismissal of an employee without valid reason is:
options: Allowed only during the probation period
questions.explanation: Article 35 prohibits the dismissal of an employee without valid reason, unless it is related to their aptitude or conduct, or based on the operational requirements of the company.

questions.question: Dr. Sidki, as an employer, must issue a work card to his employees. According to Article 23, what must it contain?
questions.explanation: Article 23 requires the employer to issue a work card containing the details set by regulation.

questions.question: According to Article 43, what is the minimum notice period for termination of a permanent contract in the absence of gross misconduct?
questions.explanation: Article 43 specifies that any clause setting the notice period at less than eight days is null and void. The minimum period is therefore 8 days.

questions.question: According to Article 52, an employee is entitled to severance pay after how many months of work?
questions.explanation: Article 52 provides that an employee bound by an indefinite-term contract is entitled to severance pay in the event of dismissal after six months of work in the same company.

questions.question: According to Article 53, how many hours of salary does the severance pay represent for the first 5 years of seniority?
questions.explanation: Article 53 sets the severance pay at 96 hours of salary for the first five years of seniority.

questions.question: According to Article 184, what is the normal working hours for non-agricultural activities in Morocco?
questions.explanation: Article 184 sets the normal working hours for non-agricultural activities at 2288 hours per year or 44 hours per week.

questions.question: According to Article 201, overtime worked between 6am and 9pm entitles to a supplement of:
questions.explanation: Article 201 provides for a 25% supplement for overtime worked between 6am and 9pm in non-agricultural activities.

questions.question: According to Article 152, what is the duration of maternity leave for an employee?
questions.explanation: Article 152 provides for maternity leave of fourteen weeks, unless more favorable provisions are provided in the employment contract or collective agreement.

questions.question: According to Article 231, after how many months of continuous service is the employee entitled to paid annual leave?
questions.explanation: Article 231 provides that after six months of continuous service, every employee is entitled to paid annual leave.

questions.question: According to Article 231, the duration of paid annual leave is:
questions.explanation: Article 231 sets the duration of paid annual leave at one and a half days of actual work per month of service.

questions.question: According to Article 153, for how many weeks after childbirth can the employee not be employed?
questions.explanation: Article 153 provides that employees who have given birth cannot be employed during the period of seven consecutive weeks following childbirth.

questions.question: According to Article 346, what discrimination in wages is prohibited?
options: Discrimination based on sex for work of equal value
Discrimination based on region of origin
questions.explanation: Article 346 prohibits any discrimination in wages between the two sexes for work of equal value.

questions.question: According to Article 362, wages must be paid in:
options: Any currency chosen by the employer
questions.explanation: Article 362 provides that wages must be paid in Moroccan currency notwithstanding any contrary clause.

questions.question: According to Article 363, workers must be paid at least:
options: Twice a month at a maximum interval of sixteen days
questions.explanation: Article 363 provides that wages must be paid at least twice a month, at a maximum interval of sixteen days, to workers.

questions.question: According to Article 72, the employer must issue a work certificate to the employee within a maximum period of:
questions.explanation: Article 72 requires the employer to issue a work certificate within a maximum period of eight days, under penalty of damages.
